acceptance: src/features/weekly_radar/domain/system_health.rs exposes public provider-agnostic SystemHealth, HealthStatus, EvidenceCoverage, DegradedCompany, SourceCoverage, ExtractionFailure, and Freshness facts; constructors reject blank text and invalid percentage values deterministically without deriving health status.

EvidenceCoverage and SourceCoverage retain supplied available, expected, and percentage values exactly; source coverage is ordered and duplicate source identities are rejected without mutating the collection.
DegradedCompany and ExtractionFailure retain supplied company/source, identity, reason, and failure facts in insertion order; duplicate company or failure identities are rejected deterministically.

SystemHealth retains the explicitly supplied HealthStatus and Freshness, exposes all five health sections, and does not recompute status from counts, failures, freshness, Stage, Ranking, or any other feature output.

WeeklyRadarPublication can carry at most one typed SystemHealth section while retaining the existing snapshot identity and publication facts; the application Publisher API remains unchanged and provider-agnostic.
The Domain implementation imports no Telegram, HTTP, Secret, network, database, Scheduler, or other feature module; no shared architecture test or global coverage policy is changed.

Focused, module-local, companion, and public integration tests cover explicit fact retention, duplicate rejection, invalid input, no health recomputation, publication binding, and provider-agnostic compilation.

The WI spec, implementation plan, reference-impact evidence, active Summary, strict AI Cockpit Finish evidence, archive bundle, and local commit record the delivered boundary, verification, remaining scope, and user authorization.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Keep Weekly Radar Domain independent of Telegram, HTTP, Secret, network, database, Scheduler, persistence, rendering, and external providers.
Consume only explicitly supplied facts; never derive HealthStatus, Stage, Ranking, Top5, or a trading/capital action.
Preserve supplied collection order and reject duplicate identities without replacing earlier facts.
Do not add dependencies or modify shared architecture tests, global coverage policy, or unrelated Work Items.
Resolve issues within this Work Item when they remain inside its Contract scope; do not broaden the boundary silently.

intent.problem: Weekly Radar has a typed snapshot/publication boundary but no structured, provider-agnostic place to publish evidence coverage, degraded companies, source coverage, extraction failures, freshness, and an explicit system health status. Without that boundary, later renderers could either lose these facts or re-derive them from unrelated Stage/Ranking outputs.
constraints: Health facts enter WeeklyRadarPublication through a Domain boundary whose provider integration surface is excluded.
HealthStatus remains an upstream explicit fact; counts, source coverage, extraction failures, freshness, Stage, and Ranking are retained as independent inputs.

The declared change set is limited to Weekly Radar Domain, tests, docs, reference-impact evidence, and generated Work Item evidence; shared architecture tests and global coverage policy remain unchanged.
The current WI lifecycle ends with strict Finish, Archive, and a local commit; external repository publication actions are outside this execution.
intent.rationale: A typed SystemHealth section keeps health data auditable and reusable by future Markdown/Telegram renderers while preserving the existing publication contract and a clean Domain/Application/Infrastructure separation.
